intro: Two more subordinators, for how and with what result. indem answers Wie? — by doing what: Ich spare Geld, indem ich selbst koche (by cooking myself); Man lernt eine Sprache, indem man sie spricht. English uses 'by + -ing'; German uses a full clause with the verb at the end and the same subject on both sides. sodass (also written so dass) gives the consequence: Es regnete stark, sodass die Straße gesperrt wurde (so that / with the result that). When the cause is an adjective or adverb, the so moves in front of it and dass follows: Er war so müde, dass er einschlief. These two, with damit and um … zu, weil and obwohl, complete the core set of adverbial clauses; whenever you suggest a solution, indem shines — 'Man kann das Problem lösen, indem man …' is the standard proposal sentence.
tips[0].title: indem = by …-ing (means)
tips[0].text: Ich spare Geld, indem ich selbst koche. Sie bleibt fit, indem sie Rad fährt. Wie? → indem. Verb at the end; the same subject in both clauses (or man).
tips[0].trap: 'by cooking' has no subject; German must add one: indem ich koche. And indem is not 'in dem' (in which): das Haus, in dem ich wohne.
tips[0].check.why: Listening is how he improves, the means, so it is indem, written as one word.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].a: Er lernt, indem er Podcasts hört.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].b: Es regnete stark, sodass das Spiel ausfiel.
tips[1].title: sodass = with the result that
tips[1].text: Der Bus kam zu spät, sodass wir den Zug verpassten. Es war laut, sodass ich nicht schlafen konnte. The result follows; verb at the end. sodass and so dass are both accepted spellings.
tips[1].check.why: Missing the appointment is the result, and the verb is at the end, so it needs sodass. deshalb would need the verb second.
tips[2].title: so + adjective, dass …
tips[2].text: Er war so müde, dass er einschlief. Der Film war so langweilig, dass wir gingen. When the cause is a degree (so tired, so boring), split it: so before the adjective, dass after the comma.
tips[2].check.why: so already stands before the adjective, so only dass follows the comma.
tips[3].title: sodass looks forward; deshalb looks the same way with verb second
tips[3].text: Es regnete, sodass die Straße gesperrt wurde. = Es regnete, deshalb wurde die Straße gesperrt. Same result, subordinate (verb last) vs main clause (verb second).
tips[3].check.why: The verb blieben comes straight after the gap, in position 2, so you need the adverb deshalb. sodass would send it to the end.
remember[0]: indem = by doing (how); sodass = with the result that.
remember[1]: so + adjective, dass: split the so.
mistakes[0].why: Means with a verb needs an indem-clause.
mistakes[1].why: With so before the adjective, use dass.
mistakes[2].why: sodass sends the verb to the end.
hook: Explain how you manage things and what follows from them: indem for 'by doing', sodass for 'and so'.
